backlogMapping.note: File ownership below is the backlog's per-round ownership (docs/atlas-backlog-2026-10-04.md 'Proposed rounds'), re-checked against main. Where v1 and the backlog differ, the backlog wins and the difference is listed in changesFromV1.

changesFromV1: R1 Maithea does NOT get whiter. v1 expected 68.8% -> about 76% snow because 72% of its land was above 4 km. On terrain-1.8.0-relief Maithea land p50 is 427 m (p90 2694, p99 4331, max 5760 m) and snow is 19.5% (classifier label, 60k directions). Prototype M1 gives 20.2% (label) / 21.0% (onset). v1 open question 1 is retired: the owner already set the 15-40% band (owner decision 1, 2026-10-03), pinned in tests/terrain-relief-hypsometry.test.mjs.

R2 Lethuris: v1 expected 90% -> about 71%. Now 20.0% (label; onset 42.9%) -> prototype 10.6% (label) / 11.8% (onset). Its effective obliquity is 70.8 deg, so the large seasonal range melts snow under PDD. Lethuris also has 22.4% of land with Tw > 316 K (polar summers).

R3 Selawyn: v1 quoted warmest month 376 K and 37% snow. Now: snow 0%, effective obliquity 89.8 deg (ITCZ at the pole), max Tw 388.8 K -> prototype 345.3 K, Tw > 316 K on 91.4% of land, forestSuitability01 > 0.5 on 48.7% of land -> 2.4% (heat cap, shipped moisture) / 3.7% (heat cap, PET moisture). The 'sterile hot' class covers 50.7% (shipped climate) / 43.0% (prototype) of land.

R5 Heat, not snow, is now the dominant M1 effect on the corpus. Corpus of 721 life-eligible rocky planets (W0-CLIMATE definition: temperateHabitat bodies in the first 2000 systems of LETHRA-001 G001 from sector x=266, 8000 directions each, land >= 1%): 448 of 721 have > 5% of land with Tw > 316 K. Forest > 0.5 median 42.4% -> 12.0% under the heat cap. Snow median 6.5% -> 3.3%.

R6 311 of 721 corpus planets have the ITCZ (argmax of the annual-mean insolation table, itczLatDeg in the probe) at a pole; 310 of them have effective obliquity > 54 deg, and G001/C2134,7,5/0/planet/1 (obliquity 53.899 deg) is polar too, so acceptance selects by the ITCZ, never by obliquity. 50 of the 132-planet set have obliquity > 54 deg. The v1 'high-tilt synthetic world' check is therefore not an edge case: it becomes a corpus-level acceptance (P1 step 6).

R7 Snow threshold ambiguity in v1. The v1 snow tables and ELA anchors used PDD < 250 (= snowFraction > 0, onset), while the classifier and every test count snow as snowFraction > 0.6 ('Alpine / polar snow'), which under the v1 ramp is PDD < 190. v2 reports both and defines every acceptance on the label (snowFraction > 0.6).

R8 Earth ELA under prototype M1, label definition: equator 4608, 45 deg 3003, 60 deg 1505, 70 deg 719, 78 deg 426 m (onset: 4561 / 2899 / 1399 / 611 / 317). All inside the v1 bands. Without the warm-column correction the equator is 4302 m on the label (4258 m onset), both < 4450, so step 2 stays mandatory. The shipped rule gives label 5674 / 2726 / 810 / 0 / 0 and onset 5120 / 2172 / 256 / 0 / 0 m.

R9 SITE_A moved in the relief round (tests/harness-sites.mjs, SITE_A_M [4075043.7, -1510938.2, 2845723.8]; v1 used the legacy site). New site: ground 280.2 m, latitude 16.9 deg, inside the fixed dry belt (dryBelt01 = 1) but effectiveMoisture 0.750, forestPotential true. Eco class 6 (humid subtropical) under both the shipped and the prototype climate (Ta 294.91 K, Tw 299.22 K, Tc 290.60 K). Tc is only 0.55 K below the tropical-wet threshold 291.15 K: a 12.7% cut of the seasonal half-range moves it to class 7. M2 continentality will very likely do that (the maritime factor is 0.792 today; at 0.6 Tc = 291.65 K). That 0.55 K / 12.7% figure holds for the shipped moisture. Under the prototype the site's effective moisture is 0.532 (uncalibrated PET), below both class 7's 0.62 threshold (so a Tc crossing would give class 8, savanna, also outside {4,5,6}) and SITE_RULE.minMoisture 0.6 (tests/harness-sites.mjs:33): with uncalibrated moisture SITE_A already fails SITE_RULE after M1. Whether it still fails after calibration is not known. The v1 STOP condition will very likely fire at M1 or M2 unless the owner decides first: new open question Q2.

R10 The v1 eco-identity gate (a 60 km ring of 64 points around SITE_A) is unusable on relief terrain: 15 of 64 points are ocean, and the SHIPPED climate already puts 18 ring points in class 7 and 6 in class 11 (prototype: 19 in class 8). v2 uses the SITE_RULE rings instead (0.5 / 1 / 2 km x 32, tests/harness-sites.mjs). At 2 km all 32 points are land and in {4, 6} under both climates.

R11 The v1 herd target ('Maithea mean land herd weight 0.27 -> >= 0.40') is already met on relief terrain: mean land weights[1] is 0.787 and mean herd habitability weights[1]*(0.4+0.6*moisture) is 0.548. Per eco class on Maithea the HABITABILITY term (the probe does not run herd placement or species eligibility, so this is the presence ceiling, not measured presence) is near zero only in class 0 nival (mean 0.017; 88% of its points below 0.02) and low in class 11 coast (0.205); tundra 0.553, hot desert 0.547, cold desert 0.537, alpine 0.658. Same pattern on Lethuris and Selawyn. P6's eco path therefore matters most for nival/ice-margin and coast; the target is replaced by a per-class presence gate measured on actual herd placement.

R12 P2's geophysics half shipped in the relief round (src/planet-geophysics.ts, planet-geophysics-1, docs/planet-geophysics-v1.md). It is wired: lapse-rate gravity (surface-climate-1.1-geo-g) and the relief scale tau. The relief preview and the absolute-height-gate prerequisites are done (surface-biomes-2.1-sea-datum: sand, 'Coastal sand', forest strip and climate datum are all measured from the current sea level). P2 is reduced to the climate grid.

R13 The v1 grid land-height proxy max(0, (macro - sea) * 47000) no longer describes the land. Land p50 / p90 / p99 on Maithea (grid-part sample): proxy 4670 / 10388 / 14408 m vs ground 426 / 2691 / 4361 m; Spearman rank correlation with the ground height 0.614 (Lethuris 0.548). The relief floor without detail (reliefLayersSampler smoothFloorM) correlates 0.984 (Lethuris 0.975). The rain-shadow rise must come from a relief-consistent height. surface-climate.ts cannot import terrain.ts (terrain.ts already imports the climate and classifier modules: cycle), so the grid takes an injected land-height function (P2) and M2 chooses the provider (P1 step 8). The macro ocean mask (macro < sea) disagrees with the real ocean flag on 0.4% of directions on Maithea and Lethuris; accepted at grid scale.

R14 The uncalibrated PET prototype makes land wetter, not drier: Maithea effM median 0.484 -> 0.599, hot-desert class 4.9% -> 0.4%. This confirms v1 risk (a): the zonal band must be calibrated before anything is pinned. Acceptance stays on the Earth reference targets.

R15 Budgets. Contended best-of-N on main: surfaceClimate 141 ns, biomeClassifier 253 ns, climateForcingFor cold 1.77 ms (v1 quoted 95 / 135 ns at b0f3882). Absolute nanosecond gates are not reproducible on this shared host, so v2 states gates as an interleaved A/B ratio against main in one process, and keeps the absolute values as quiet-host targets for task 20.

R16 New coupling v1 did not know: tests/terrain-relief-hypsometry.test.mjs pins owner decision 1 (Maithea snow 15-40%, snow on >= 20% of land above 3 km at |lat| < 60, <= 5% snow on land below 1.5 km, corpus132 median <= 20%, <= 20 planets above 90%, bin medians falling with anchor temperature). workPackages.changes:
As v1 P1 steps 1-9, with these corrections.
M1 (no dependencies):
1) PDD kernel exactly as v1 (tabulated H(v) and G(v), detAcos only at module init). snowFraction = clamp01((PDD_CRIT - pdd0)/PDD_RAMP), PDD_CRIT 250, PDD_RAMP 100. State in the doc that the label 'Alpine / polar snow' (snowFraction > 0.6) is PDD < 190 and that ELA tests use the label.
2) Warm-column lapse as v1 (mandatory: without it the Earth equator ELA is 4302 m label / 4258 m onset).
3) Warmest-month ceiling as v1.
4) Heat cap as v1. Expected (prototype): Selawyn forest > 0.5 48.7% -> 2-4%, Raiva 47.8% -> 6-10%, corpus median 42% -> 12%. Owner-visible: Q6.
5) PET effective moisture as v1, CALIBRATED: the uncalibrated band makes land wetter (Maithea effM median 0.484 -> 0.599, hot desert 4.9% -> 0.4%).
6) ITCZ zonal band as v1. 311 of the 721 corpus planets have the ITCZ at a pole, including Selawyn (89.8), Lethuris (70.8) and Raiva (61.4), so the polar-ITCZ branch is a main path, tested on the corpus (acceptance 2).
7) Versions/doc as v1 except: CLIMATE_VERSION 'surface-climate-1.1-geo-g' -> 'surface-climate-2'; do NOT touch terrain.ts (the coordinator bumps TERRAIN_VERSION); TREE_HABITAT_VERSION 'tree-habitat-2-climate' -> 'tree-habitat-3-heat'.
M2 (after P2 has merged):
8) Wire the grid. buildClimateGrid needs a relief-consistent land-height function (R13). surface-climate.ts must not import terrain.ts (cycle). Choose ONE and document it: (a) climate-grid.ts (owned by P2 in round A; ownership passes to P1 for M2 after P2 has merged, see ownsFiles) reimplements the macro relief floor of terrain-1.8.0-relief (compressed continental term + tau plateau steps + ridge belt, no hills/gullies/rocks) from catalog.ts noise and the R-CAL-1 constants copied with a parity test against reliefLayersSampler(body).smoothFloorM on Maithea and Lethuris over 10k land directions: max |difference| <= 1 m (it is a copy of the same field, so the bound is tight; rank correlation alone would allow a wrong height scale) and a sha check that the copied constants equal terrain.ts RELIEF_CALIBRATION; or (b) the forcing takes an injected provider set by a module that may import terrain.ts, with the cache key unchanged and a seek-independence test. (a) is recommended (no new import edge). forcingForBody's parity check (surface-biomes.ts:45) compares g, which already depends on radius through planet-geophysics; add radiusM explicitly anyway, because the grid reads it. SITE_A guard as v1 but with the COMPLETE SITE_RULE (moisture >= 0.6, height, forestPotential, rings) and the legacy class set, checked after M1 and after M2; see Q2: SITE_A is 0.55 K from the class-7 Tc threshold (a maritime factor below about 0.69 crosses it, giving class 7 or 8 depending on moisture), and the uncalibrated M1 moisture 0.532 already fails minMoisture 0.6.
M3 (after P3 has merged): classifier v3 fields as v1. BIOME_VERSION 'surface-biomes-2.1-sea-datum' -> 'surface-biomes-3-eco'; SURVEY_VERSION 'surface-survey-2.1-relief' -> 'surface-survey-3'. Height inputs to eco-class.ts are heights above the current sea level / climate datum (R19).
acceptance: Earth reference (tests/climate-earth-reference.test.mjs, 288 K, 23.44 deg, water 0.7, g 9.81), ELA = lowest height with snowFraction > 0.6: 45 deg 2700-3100 m, 60 deg 1200-1700 m, 70 deg 550-1000 m, 78 deg 250-650 m, equator >= 4450 m (prototype: 3003, 1505, 719, 426, 4608). A negative test running the shipped annual-mean rule fails the 60 deg band (it gives 810 m label / 256 m onset). Zonal moisture targets as v1 step 6. After M2, continentality targets as v1 step 8.

Polar ITCZ: on a synthetic 70 deg world the wettest zonal band is poleward and the driest band moves with it. On the 721 corpus, select planets by the ITCZ itself (itczLatDeg > 45; 311 today), not by obliquity. For every selected planet with >= 50 land samples (8000 directions) both within 10 deg of the ITCZ and 18-35 deg from it (213 today), the land-mean effM near the ITCZ must be >= that of the 18-35 deg band; ANY failure blocks the package (listed by id). expectedOutcomes:
Measured basis: measuredBaseline (prototype M1 where stated; the zonal band is uncalibrated, so moisture-driven numbers will move after calibration and after M2).

Snow: Earth ELAs land inside the Earth bands. Maithea stays about 20% snow (owner band 15-40%) with more snow on the ranges (28.7% -> about 36% of land above 3 km at |lat| < 60). Lethuris falls from 20% to about 11%. Selawyn and Raiva stay snow-free. Corpus median 6.5% -> about 3%.

Heat: hot and high-tilt worlds lose most of their forest. Selawyn's warmest month falls from 389 K to about 345 K but stays above 316 K on about 92% of its land, so the heat cap removes good forest from nearly all of it (48.7% -> about 3%). That is forest suppression, not class assignment: under the v1 rule order only 43.1% of Selawyn's land is classed hot desert or sterile hot, and 27.5% keeps a forest class with Tw' >= 316 K (R21, P3 decides). Corpus forest > 0.5 median 42% -> about 12%.

Biomes: Maithea already spans every class 0-11 on the shipped climate (nival 19.5, steppe 18.8, savanna 12.9, temperate forest 9.5, alpine 8.0, boreal 5.8, tropical wet 5.6, cold desert 5.3, hot desert 4.9, humid subtropical 4.6, tundra 4.4, coast 0.7%). The increment's job there is to make them distinguishable (P4) and correctly placed (calibrated moisture, continentality), not to create them.

Life: the habitability term is already high in every Maithea class except the nival margin and the coast (actual presence not measured). P6 adds the ice-margin and coast herds and the ecotype phenotypes.

Harness: SITE_A is class 6 today; it will probably leave the legacy set or fail SITE_RULE moisture at M1 or M2 (Q2).
openQuestionsForUser: Q1 RETIRED. 'Maithea gets whiter (76%)' no longer applies: relief already lowered Maithea's snow to 19.6% and the owner set the 15-40% band (decision 1, 2026-10-03). Prototype M1 keeps it at about 20%.

Q2 NEW. The life/forest harness site SITE_A is humid subtropical (class 6) but its coldest month is only 0.55 K below the tropical threshold. Adding continentality (M2) will very likely cross it; the site then becomes tropical wet (class 7) if moisture stays >= 0.62, or savanna (class 8) if moisture falls, as the uncalibrated PET does (0.532). Both are outside the legacy-behaviour set {4,5,6} the life identity relies on. Separately, the uncalibrated M1 moisture already breaks SITE_RULE.minMoisture 0.6; calibration may or may not restore it. Options: (a) move the harness site with the existing deterministic search after M1 and again after M2, adding 'centre and rings in {4,5,6} with >= 1 K Tc margin' to SITE_RULE, and keep REFERENCE e6a0b39; (b) add classes 7 and 8 to the legacy-behaviour set, so those cells keep increment-1 life behaviour everywhere (does not fix the moisture rule); (c) bend the climate to keep the site (rejected: physics is never retuned for a test). Recommended: (a). State: OPEN.

Q3 PARTLY DECIDED. Surface physics already uses per-planet geophysics gravity (owner decisions 3 and 4, relief round). Still open: whether catalogue masses should ever follow (moves moons, orbits and bookmarks). Recommended: no, not in this increment. State: OPEN.

Q4 UNCHANGED, MORE URGENT. Day lengths are a placeholder (3 h to 200 d), so wind-belt width is fixed at 30 deg from the ITCZ. 311 of 721 corpus planets have the ITCZ at a pole, so this placeholder shapes almost half the corpus. Recommended: keep 30 deg this increment; redraw spin later as its own versioned change. State: OPEN.
Q5 UNCHANGED. Dry planets with air (hasAir is queryable since planet-geophysics-1 but does not feed the biosphere) still have no life. Recommended: a later version-bumped step. State: OPEN.

Q6 NEW, owner-visible consequence. The heat cap removes most forest from hot and high-tilt worlds: Selawyn 48.7% -> about 3% of land with good forest, Raiva 47.8% -> about 6-10%, corpus median 42% -> about 12%. Lethuris snow falls 20% -> about 11%. Ship as physics and say so plainly? Recommended: yes. State: OPEN.
